subject: Leadership comms: role transitions and QBR-ready messaging
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: leadership comms + role transitions for Q3 org update

Team —

Attached are two artifacts to start: a proposed org chart (org_chart_v1.pdf) and a short set of QBR talking points (qbr_talking_points_v3.docx). High level proposal below — looking for objections, edits, and any people/compensation/legal blockers we should surface before we finalize an exec draft.

Summary of changes (proposed):
- Combine Serving and Platform into a single "Runtime" org (reporting to Senior Director, Runtime). Objective: reduce handoffs around kernel selection, deployment config, and latency SLO ownership.
- Create a new Senior TPM role (Customer Runtime) to own cross-customer rollout playbooks and QA for dedicated/private deployments.
- Move two individual contributors (infra SREs) from Platform into Runtime lead to centralize low-latency ops.
- Transition an existing manager (TBD) to be interim head of Product for Dedicated for 90 days during recruitment.

Why now:
- QBR narrative needs a clear line between product work (model-agnostic serving primitives) and runtime ops (latency/reliability).
- Metrics show variance in tail latency where ownership is unclear. Consolidation should give us a single owner for end-to-end SLOs.

Risks & asks:
- People impact: we must surface manager reassignments, scope changes, and any comp/level questions to People before internal announcement.
- Partners/Customers: Acme (Sarah Lim) is in pilot for Dedicated; we should offer a private heads-up before company-wide comms.

Proposed timeline:
- 7/14: Exec review of final comms (this thread -> exec list)
- 7/16: Publish manager-level talking points and FAQ to managers
- 7/21: Company-wide announcement post-QBR

Please review the attachments and reply with: (1) substantive edits to top-level bullets; (2) any blocking HR/legal items; (3) suggested changes to timeline.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
VP, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: org_chart_v1.pdf (diagram), qbr_talking_points_v3.docx (draft)

Jonas —

Thanks for starting this. A few inline thoughts (high level first):

- Tone: recommend we lead with a people-first framing. Instead of "consolidate to reduce handoffs" say "align teams to accelerate reliability and reduce friction for customers."
- Sequence: we need to confirm manager moves with People and ensure no surprises to direct reports. That should be a gating item before any external notice.
- FAQ: add a short section (1 page) that managers can use in 1:1s — likely questions on comp, individual IC scope, and reporting lines.

Inline: 
> - Create a new Senior TPM role (Customer Runtime) to own cross-customer rollout playbooks and QA for dedicated/private deployments.

Suggest: "Senior TPM (Customer Runtime) — focused on rollout playbooks, post-launch metrics, and customer beta coordination."

> - Transition an existing manager (TBD) to be interim head of Product for Dedicated for 90 days during recruitment.

Suggest we remove "TBD" from the managers memo and instead say "interim leader (to be named after People confirmation)" so managers can explain the process to their teams.

Legal/People flags:
- People will need a list of affected roles and proposed reporting dates.
- If there are level changes or promo/comp adjustments we must include timing and approvals.

I'll add manager talking points and a draft FAQ and send back by Monday (7/13).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
